title: Uniform provisions concerning the measures to be taken against the emission of gaseous and particulate pollutants from compression-ignition engines and positive-ignition engines (fuelled with petrol, LPG, natural gas/biomethane, ethanol, hydrogen, including dual-fuel) for use in vehicles, and vehicles with regard to emissions
scope_summary: Approves heavy-duty engine systems and engine families as separate technical units, vehicles with an approved engine system, and vehicles as a whole with regard to gaseous and particulate pollutant emissions, smoke, OBD, NOx control measures and engine installation. It also approves replacement pollution control devices as separate technical units, for motor vehicles of categories M1, M2, N1 and N2 with a reference mass above 2,610 kg and all M3 and N3 vehicles, with optional extensions down to 2,380 kg.
scope_quote: This Regulation shall apply to motor vehicles of categories M1, M2, N1 and N2 with a reference mass exceeding 2,610 kg and to all motor vehicles of categories M3 and N3. At the request of the manufacturer, the type approval of a completed vehicle given under this Regulation shall be extended to its incomplete vehicle with a reference mass below 2,610 kg. [...] The following do not need to be approved according to this Regulation: engines mounted in vehicles of up to 2,840 kg reference mass to which an approval to UN Regulation No. 83 or UN Regulation No. 154 has been granted.

defined_terms.label: Engine approval
defined_terms.definition: Approval of an engine type (engine family) with regard to gaseous and particulate pollutant emissions, smoke and the OBD system.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle approval
defined_terms.definition: Approval of a vehicle type with regard to engine emissions, smoke, OBD system and engine installation on the vehicle.

defined_terms.label: Auxiliary Emission Strategy
defined_terms.definition: An emission strategy that replaces or modifies the base emission strategy in response to specific ambient/operating conditions and only while those conditions exist.

defined_terms.label: Base Emission Strategy
defined_terms.definition: An emission strategy active throughout the engine speed and load range unless an AES is activated.

defined_terms.label: Crankcase
defined_terms.definition: Spaces in or external to an engine connected to the oil sump through which gases and vapours can be emitted.

defined_terms.label: Critical emission-related components
defined_terms.definition: Components designed primarily for emission control: any exhaust aftertreatment system, the ECU and its associated sensors and actuators, and the EGR system including filters, coolers, control valves and tubing.

defined_terms.label: Defeat strategy
defined_terms.definition: An emission strategy that does not meet the performance requirements for a base and/or auxiliary emission strategy.

defined_terms.label: deNOx system
defined_terms.definition: An exhaust aftertreatment system designed to reduce NOx emissions (e.g. lean NOx catalysts, NOx adsorbers, SCR systems).

defined_terms.label: Diagnostic trouble code
defined_terms.definition: A numeric or alphanumeric identifier which identifies or labels a malfunction.

defined_terms.label: Diesel mode
defined_terms.definition: Normal operating mode of a dual-fuel engine in which no gaseous fuel is used under any operating condition.

defined_terms.label: Dual-fuel engine
defined_terms.definition: An engine system designed to operate simultaneously on diesel fuel and a gaseous fuel, both metered separately, with variable relative consumption.

defined_terms.label: Dual-fuel mode
defined_terms.definition: Normal operating mode of a dual-fuel engine in which it simultaneously uses diesel and gaseous fuel at some operating conditions.

defined_terms.label: Dual-fuel vehicle
defined_terms.definition: A vehicle powered by a dual-fuel engine supplying the fuels from separate on-board storage systems.

defined_terms.label: Element of design
defined_terms.definition: Any element of the engine system, any control system (software, electronic control systems, computer logic), any control calibration, or results of system interactions.

defined_terms.label: Emission control monitoring system
defined_terms.definition: The system ensuring correct operation of the NOx control measures implemented in the engine system per paragraph 5.5.

defined_terms.label: Emission control system
defined_terms.definition: The elements of design and emission strategies developed or calibrated for the purpose of controlling emissions.

defined_terms.label: Emission strategy
defined_terms.definition: An element or set of elements of design incorporated into an engine system or vehicle and used in controlling emissions.

defined_terms.label: Engine aftertreatment system family
defined_terms.definition: Engines of an engine family further grouped by similar exhaust aftertreatment system.

defined_terms.label: Engine family
defined_terms.definition: A manufacturer's grouping of engines with similar exhaust emission characteristics by design as defined in paragraph 7.

defined_terms.label: Engine system
defined_terms.definition: The engine, the emission control system and the communication interface between the engine ECU(s) and any other powertrain or vehicle control unit.

defined_terms.label: Engine type
defined_terms.definition: A category of engines not differing in essential engine characteristics as set out in Annex 1.

defined_terms.label: Exhaust aftertreatment system
defined_terms.definition: A catalyst, particulate filter, deNOx system, combined deNOx particulate filter or any other emission reducing device installed downstream of the engine.

defined_terms.label: Gaseous pollutants
defined_terms.definition: Exhaust emissions of CO, NOx (as NO2) and hydrocarbons (THC, NMHC, methane).

defined_terms.label: In-use performance ratio
defined_terms.definition: Ratio of the number of times monitor conditions existed to detect a malfunction relative to the number of relevant driving cycles.

defined_terms.label: Malfunction
defined_terms.definition: A failure or deterioration of an engine system, including OBD, expected to increase regulated pollutants or reduce OBD effectiveness.

defined_terms.label: Malfunction indicator
defined_terms.definition: An indicator, part of the alert system, that clearly informs the driver of a malfunction.

defined_terms.label: Net power
defined_terms.definition: Power at the crankshaft end on a test bench with auxiliaries per UN R85 under reference atmospheric conditions.

defined_terms.label: On-board diagnostic system
defined_terms.definition: An on-board system able to detect emission-relevant malfunctions, indicate them via an alert system and identify and communicate the likely malfunction area off-board.

defined_terms.label: OBD engine family
defined_terms.definition: A grouping of engine systems with common methods of monitoring and diagnosing emission-related malfunctions.

defined_terms.label: Original pollution control device
defined_terms.definition: A pollution control device or assembly covered by the type-approval granted for the vehicle concerned.

defined_terms.label: Parent engine
defined_terms.definition: An engine selected from an engine family as representative of its emission characteristics.

defined_terms.label: Particulate aftertreatment device
defined_terms.definition: An exhaust aftertreatment system reducing particulate pollutants by mechanical, aerodynamic, diffusional or inertial separation.

defined_terms.label: Particulate matter
defined_terms.definition: Material collected on a specified filter medium after diluting exhaust to 315–325 K.

defined_terms.label: Particulate Matter number
defined_terms.definition: Total number of solid particles emitted from the exhaust, quantified per Annex 4.

defined_terms.label: Portable emissions measurement system
defined_terms.definition: A portable emissions measurement system meeting Appendix 2 to Annex 8.

defined_terms.label: Power take-off unit
defined_terms.definition: An engine driven output device for powering auxiliary vehicle-mounted equipment.

defined_terms.label: Qualified deteriorated component or system
defined_terms.definition: A component or system intentionally deteriorated and accepted by the authority for demonstrating OBD performance per Annex 9B.

defined_terms.label: Reagent
defined_terms.definition: Any medium stored on-board in a tank and provided to the exhaust aftertreatment system upon request of the emission control system.

defined_terms.label: Recalibration
defined_terms.definition: Fine tuning of a natural gas engine to provide the same performance in a different range of natural gas.

defined_terms.label: Reference mass
defined_terms.definition: Mass in running order less 75 kg driver mass plus a uniform 100 kg.

defined_terms.label: Replacement pollution control device
defined_terms.definition: A pollution control device or assembly intended to replace an original one, approvable as a separate technical unit.

defined_terms.label: Scan-tool
defined_terms.definition: External test equipment for standardised off-board communication with the OBD system.

defined_terms.label: Service mode
defined_terms.definition: A special mode of a dual-fuel engine activated for repair or moving the vehicle when dual-fuel mode operation is not possible.

defined_terms.label: Tampering
defined_terms.definition: Inactivation, adjustment or modification of the emissions control or propulsion system, including software, that worsens emissions performance.

defined_terms.label: Useful life
defined_terms.definition: Period of distance and/or time over which compliance with emission limits must be assured.

defined_terms.term: vehicle type with regard to emissions
defined_terms.label: Vehicle type with regard to emissions
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles not differing in essential engine and vehicle characteristics as set out in Annex 1.

defined_terms.label: Wall flow Diesel Particulate Filter
defined_terms.definition: A DPF in which all exhaust gas is forced through a wall that filters out solid matter.

defined_terms.label: Wobbe index
defined_terms.definition: Ratio of the calorific value of a gas per unit volume to the square root of its relative density.

defined_terms.label: λ-shift factor
defined_terms.definition: Expression of required engine management flexibility regarding excess-air ratio when fuelled with gas differing from pure methane.

defined_terms.label: Periodic regeneration
defined_terms.definition: Regeneration of an emission control device occurring periodically in less than 100 hours of normal operation.

defined_terms.label: Continuous regeneration
defined_terms.definition: Regeneration of an aftertreatment system occurring permanently or at least once per WHTC hot start test.

applicability_hints: The engine ECU and all its associated sensors and actuators are 'critical emission-related components', so any engine control sensor/actuator falls under R49 OBD, durability and anti-tampering requirements

Aftermarket catalytic converters, deNOx devices (SCR) and particulate filters for heavy-duty engines/vehicles must be type-approved as replacement pollution control devices under Annex 13; original replacement parts need only Annex 13 paragraphs 2.1–2.3
EGR filters, coolers, control valves and tubing count as critical emission-related components

AdBlue/urea reagent tanks, dosing systems, reagent quality and level sensors, heaters for freeze protection, and driver warning/inducement functions (incl. instrument cluster displays and torque/speed limitation) are covered by Annex 11
Engine control software and calibrations are 'elements of design'; reprogramming facilities and anti-tampering measures must be documented

Turbochargers/boost pressure control, VVT, fuel injection system, engine cooling (thermostat), oxygen/NOx/exhaust gas sensors and idle speed control are OBD-monitored components per Annex 9B Appendix 3
Gas fuel system components and labels near the fuel filling aperture are relevant for CNG/LNG/LPG engines with restricted fuel range approval
Petrol/E85 fuel tank filler inlet design is regulated (paragraph 6.3)
Dual-fuel conversion systems and hydrogen engines are covered (Annex 15, paragraph 3.5)
ECU must provide data stream for in-service PEMS testing (paragraph 8.5, Annex 8)
Approval mark may be retrievable via the instrument cluster
Heavy N1/M1 vehicles (above 2,380/2,610 kg reference mass) and incomplete vehicles may fall under R49 instead of R83/R154; vehicles up to 2,840 kg approved to R83/R154 are exempt
Power take-off units and engine-driven auxiliaries affect emission testing configuration (Annex 4 Appendix 6)
